Security model

Explainable controls. Minimal authority.

Pactrail recommends transaction structure. It does not custody production funds, expose raw proprietary intelligence or make guarantees about counterparties.

SecurityPrinciplesData handlingContractsLimitations

Design principles

  • Policy results expire and are scoped to one transaction.
  • Every safeguard is explainable and may be overridden by the integrating application.
  • Wallet addresses are analyzed as public blockchain identifiers, not treated as personal identities.
  • The API returns derived controls rather than raw proprietary wallet datasets.

Data handling

The current release stores no wallet or agreement data. Demo evaluations are computed per request. A production implementation should encrypt persisted agreements, minimize retention and separate application records from Nansen credentials.

Escrow contracts

Prototype status: the public Deal Studio simulates funding and release. Do not send funds to any address presented by the demo.

Before mainnet use, escrow contracts require independent auditing, role tests, invariant testing, emergency controls and clearly documented resolver authority.

Limitations

Onchain history is incomplete context. Wallets may be new, rotated, compromised or controlled by multiple parties. Pactrail recommendations are safeguards—not identity verification, legal advice, credit decisions or guarantees against loss.
